sentences.text: When a DC voltage source is connected to a series resistor and capacitor, the capacitor does not charge instantly.
Instead, the voltage rises exponentially according to the differential equation solution: v(t) = Vs × (1 - e^(-t / τ)).
The parameter tau (τ = R × C) is the circuit Time Constant, measured in seconds.
After one time constant (t = 1τ), the capacitor charges to 63.2% of its final voltage.
After five time constants (t = 5τ), the capacitor is over 99.3% charged, considered fully steady state.
The 5-Tau Rule of Thumb: In practical engineering, any first-order RC or RL circuit reaches steady-state after 5τ ( v(5 tau ) = V s(1 - e to the power of -5) is approximately 99.33 % settled ).
